sources.quote: Crypto Card Available in 60+ Countries — Europe, UAE, UK & More | Kolo

sources.label: Kolo Terms of Use v3.0.0 (1 July 2026), clause 22.2.1
sources.quote: You are not permitted to acquire Digital Assets or use any KOLO Services through the Site if: 22.2.1. you are in, under the control of, or a national or resident of Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, or Syria

sources.label: Kolo blog: Best crypto card in Dubai 2026
sources.quote: Which crypto card is available in Dubai? Several. Kolo, Bybit Card UAE, Crypto.com Visa, and Oobit are the main options Dubai residents are choosing between in 2026.

notes: No complete residency list is published right now. kolo.xyz/countries is titled '60+ countries — Europe, UAE, UK' but the page currently renders only two country tiles: Albania (card and wallet icons) and Algeria (wallet icon only; the card icon is hidden, so Algeria looks wallet-only, not added to 'no'). The Help Center article 'In which countries can I use my Kolo card' (help.kolo.xyz/en/articles/13605699) is a spending (merchant-country) block-list, not a residency list, so it was not used. Terms of Use only block sanctioned countries (Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, Syria, plus any country under US/UN/EU/UK sanctions). GB: the UK blog post hedges ('Confirm current UK eligibility before starting onboarding'), but the countries page title names the UK. India and the US are not mentioned anywhere. EU set to unknown (the site currently says yes): the page title says 'Europe' but no EEA country is named, and Albania (the one European tile) is not in the EEA; G2M's validator rejects EU=yes without an EEA country in the list. Wayback Machine was unreachable from this environment. Terms PDF quote was matched against https://kolo.xyz/legal-pdf/kolo/terms-of-use (the PDF behind the terms page).

sources.label: KAST Concierge: Is the KAST Card Available in My Country?
sources.quote: You can check if KAST is available in your country during the sign-up process. If you don't see your country in the dropdown menu, we haven't launched there yet.

sources.label: KAST Cardholder Agreement (US)
sources.quote: you permanently reside outside the United States

sources.label: KAST Concierge: KAST Brazil entity update, CPF, and new Terms & Conditions
sources.quote: KAST is updating the contracting entity for users whose Country of Residence is Brazil.

notes: KAST does not publish a country list; its Terms and Help Center say the list is only shown in the app's country dropdown during KYC (Card Map also records it as 'app' mode). Only US (a US cardholder agreement whose default clause is 'you permanently reside outside the United States') and Brazil (KAST Brazil entity for Brazil residents) are confirmed from issuer pages. The Help Center's 'Apple Pay Availability for KAST Cards' article lists Apple Pay countries by registered residence (incl. UAE, UK, EEA, but also Belarus and mainland China); it is Apple's list, not a card-eligibility list, so it was not used. India: only an INR payout article exists (sending to Indian bank accounts), not residency; IN left unknown. The site's '170+ countries' refers to where the card is accepted.

sources.label: Coinbase One Card Cardholder Agreement (First Electronic Bank), effective May 11, 2026
sources.quote: a valid U.S. mailing address and residential address (if different)

sources.label: Coinbase One Card Cardholder Agreement: default and relocation
sources.quote: If you move to a state, U.S. territory, or non-U.S. territory where the Card is not offered, we may be required to close your Account. Eligibility for the Account is based in part on your state of residence

notes: US-only credit card (Amex, issued by First Electronic Bank). The agreement also lists 'you permanently reside or relocate outside of the U.S.' as a default. It says eligibility depends partly on state of residence but names no excluded states. Coinbase Help 'How to apply for a Coinbase One Card' (help.coinbase.com/en/creditcard/apply) reportedly says 'Reside in the US (excluding U.S. Territories)', but coinbase.com and help.coinbase.com returned 403 to every fetch here, so that quote is from a search snippet only and is not verified; on that basis PR, GU, VI, AS, MP would be excluded (they already fall under others='no').

sources.label: Avalanche Card FAQ: What countries are supported?
sources.quote: Avalanche Card is currently available in many U.S. states, Latin America, and the Caribbean. However, residents of the following countries and regions are not eligible to sign up: Cannot issue to residents of the following countries: Belarus, Cuba, India, Iran, Iraq, Israel, Mainland China, Nepal, Nicaragua, Nigeria, North Korea, Russia, Sri Lanka, Syria, Turkey, Ukraine, Venezuela, Vietnam

sources.label: Avalanche Card FAQ: excluded U.S. states
sources.quote: Cannot issue to the residents of the following states: Arizona, Delaware, Georgia, Idaho, Louisiana, Maryland, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, Oregon, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin

notes: The issuer names regions (US, Latin America, the Caribbean) plus an 18-country block-list. 'yes' = US + the 33 sovereign Latin American and Caribbean states minus the 3 blocked ones (Cuba, Nicaragua, Venezuela): this region-to-country mapping is mine, not an issuer list, and it matches DefiLlama's list exactly. US: 16 states excluded (AZ, DE, GA, ID, LA, MD, NV, NM, ND, OH, OR, RI, SD, VT, WA, WI). 'others' is unknown, not 'no': the block-list names non-Latin-American countries (India, Israel, China, Vietnam), so the region sentence may not be exhaustive. UAE, UK and EEA are not mentioned either way. Caribbean territories (Puerto Rico, Cayman, Aruba, etc.) were left out of 'yes'. The international card agreement adds that non-US applicants attest they are not US citizens.

sources.label: Solayer Docs: Eligibility
sources.quote: Residents or citizens of the following countries and territories are not eligible to sign up for the Solayer Card, regardless of their current place of residence

sources.label: Solayer Docs: FAQ, Supported Countries for Card Issuance
sources.quote: Solayer Pay is available in most countries except the following:

notes: Block-list (96 entries; 'Darfur' is folded into Sudan SD; 'Eritea' = Eritrea ER). The ban covers residents AND citizens. US: residents of 17 states are not eligible (AZ, DE, GA, ID, LA, MD, MT, NV, NM, ND, OH, OR, RI, SD, VT, WA, WI). Egypt is unclear: it is on the FAQ's restricted list but not on the Eligibility page. EU = yes only on a literal reading: every EEA country is blocked except Slovenia (SI) and Liechtenstein (LI), which the lists do not name. Quotes taken from the .md versions of the docs pages (docs.solayer.org/solayer-pay/eligibility.md, faq.md).

sources.label: Bleap Help Center: Am I eligible for Card?
sources.quote: we are unable to issue cards to users who either: Reside outside of the EEA or Switzerland, regardless of their nationality.

sources.label: Bleap Help Center: Am I eligible for Card? (Italy/Spain)
sources.quote: For example, residents of countries like Italy or Spain may not yet have access to Bleap cards despite holding valid residency documents.

sources.label: Bleap: Crypto card page FAQ
sources.quote: The Bleap crypto card is currently available to residents of the European Economic Area (EEA) and Latin America.

sources.label: Bleap Help Center: Requirements for Brazilian rails
sources.quote: A valid identification document from Brazil A proof of address in Brazil

notes: Help Center allow-list: EEA + Switzerland only (so others = no, and IN/AE/US/GB = no). Unclear: Italy and Spain (Help Center says residents 'may not yet have access'), and Latin America, because the card page says 'EEA and Latin America' while the Help Center says the card is not issued outside the EEA/Switzerland; Brazil residents can open an account (Brazilian ID + Brazilian proof of address) that includes 'Global spending'. The Latin America set in 'unclear' is the 20 Latin American republics (my mapping of 'Latin America'). Separately, nationals of 45 countries cannot get the card wherever they live (incl. UAE, US, Pakistan, Philippines, Turkey, Nigeria, South Africa, Panama, Cuba, Haiti, Nicaragua, Venezuela); that is a nationality rule, not residence, so not put in 'no'.

sources.label: Tangem: Tangem Pay page FAQ, Is Tangem Pay available in my country?
sources.quote: Tangem Pay is available in the US and in select countries across LATAM, APAC, MEA, and Africa. Not all countries or US states are supported.

sources.label: Tangem: Tangem Pay page, structured data (areaServed)
sources.quote: areaServed: Argentina, Antigua & Barbuda, Bahamas, ... UAE, Uganda, Zambia, United States of America (51 entries, 50 unique)

sources.label: Tangem Help Center: Getting Started & KYC
sources.quote: A residency address in one of the supported countries or US states

notes: The 50-country 'yes' list comes from the schema.org 'areaServed' markup on Tangem's own Tangem Pay page (same list on /tangem-pay/ and /tgnm-pay/). That markup is not shown as visible text, and Tangem never calls it complete, so others = unknown. The visible text names regions only and says to check in the app. GB/EU = no because the named regions (US, LATAM, APAC, MEA, Africa) leave out Europe and the list has no European country (Tangem learning-hub posts call UK/EU 'planned for 2026'); downgrade to unknown if you want issuer-explicit wording only. India is not in areaServed (Bangladesh and Pakistan are) but is not explicitly excluded, so IN = unknown. US: not all states supported, but none are named. 'Dominicana' is a duplicate of the Dominican Republic. PR, KY and TC are territories.

sources.label: Karta Personal Help Center: Who Can Get a Karta Personal Card?
sources.quote: the Karta Personal Card is available to citizens and residents of most countries, with the exception of those listed in our unsupported countries list. To get the full list of unsupported countries, please contact our Support Team

sources.label: Karta Card Terms (B2C)
sources.quote: You attest that you are not a United States citizen, and that you are signing up for a card that is intended for those outside of the United States.

notes: Karta has a block-list but does not publish it (only via Support). Only the US is confirmed excluded, from the card terms. 'Countries Where the Card Doesn't Work' (Syria, Iran, Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Ukraine, Venezuela) is about where the card can be used, not residency, so it is not in 'no'. Card Map's 'karta' (conkarta.com, US) is a different product.

sources.label: Tuyo Guides: Tuyo card availability (US states and territories)
sources.quote: The Tuyo card cannot be issued to consumers residing in these U.S. states and territories:

notes: Block-list = 27 platform-wide prohibited countries + card-issuance exceptions (adds Israel and Nicaragua) + 5 US territories (PR, VI, AS, GU, MP). Both guides were 'verified July 16, 2026 against Tuyo Prohibitions' (about.tuyo.com Notion page, which is JS-only and could not be read here). US: card not issued in 19 states + DC (AZ, DE, GA, ID, LA, MD, MS, MO, NV, NM, ND, OH, OR, RI, SD, TN, VT, WA, WI, DC). The UK is a platform-wide prohibition (tuyo.com footer: 'not intended for ... people located in the United Kingdom'). UAE and all EEA countries are not listed, so yes.
